audit_findings.title: Redeemable noncontrolling interest is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $147m at 2026-06-26; $0.49/share; 0.45% of base equity value; recurring compensation approximately $2.5m annually, computed as $147m × €0.56/€33.27
audit_findings.mechanism: The redemption claim belongs in the equity bridge; any compensation or earnings attributable to outside holders must also be removed from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The above table does not reflect redeemable noncontrolling interests of $145 million associated with our First Sensor AG (“First Sensor”) subsidiary.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated. Deducting the entire latest filed claim would reduce base value from $109.14 to about $108.65 per share and bull value from $128.02 to about $127.53, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged relative to the $209.58 price. The implied annual compensation is only about 0.11% of anchor OE.
audit_findings.action: Confirm OE is attributable solely to TEL common shareholders and deduct the latest redeemable noncontrolling-interest balance in the next bridge rerun.

audit_findings.title: Uncertain-tax claims may be an omitted senior liability
audit_findings.magnitude: $808m at FY2025 ($719m unrecognized tax benefits plus $89m interest and penalties); $2.71/share; 2.48% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any probable cash settlement not already reflected in normalized OE or tax attributes would be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The above table does not reflect unrecognized income tax benefits of $719 million and related accrued interest and penalties of $89 million, the timing of which is uncertain.
audit_findings.explanation: The amount ultimately payable remains unresolved, but even deducting the entire filed gross amount would reduce base value to about $106.43 per share and bull value to about $125.31, still far below the $209.58 market price. The latest filing also shows accrued interest and penalties falling to $44m following settlement of prior-period tax matters, so the FY2025 gross amount requires a current rollforward.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the current uncertain-tax-position rollforward, expected cash-settlement range, and usable tax-attribute offsets; deduct only the residual economic liability in a bridge rerun.

audit_findings.title: Pension funding may exceed the cost embedded in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $609m FY2025 underfunding; $2.04/share; 1.87% of base equity value; $70m expected fiscal-2026 contributions versus $40m fiscal-2025 pension cost, a $30m difference equal to 1.35% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Excess recurring cash contributions reduce OE; any unfunded obligation not captured through future OE is a claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect pension contributions to be approximately $70 million in fiscal 2026, before consideration of any voluntary contributions.
audit_findings.explanation: The possible mismatch is real, but its filed scale does not change the conclusion. Deducting the full $609m deficit would reduce base value to about $107.10 per share and bull value to about $125.98, still well below the market price. Whether the $30m expense-to-contribution difference is recurring remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension expense, mandatory contributions, deficit-repair payments, and plan assets; rerun OE for any sustainable cash-cost excess and the bridge for any remaining uncaptured deficit.

audit_findings.title: The historical anchor may not describe the current acquisition perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.3bn Richards purchase price plus $321m for two other FY2025 acquisitions; Richards contributed $179m of FY2025 sales and $5m of operating income; filed pro-forma FY2025 net income was $1,844m versus $1,842m reported; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Full-year acquired operations could increase OE, while acquisition interest, maintenance capital, working capital, integration costs, and amortization treatment could offset that increase; the mismatch enters through the anchor and forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: On April 1, 2025, we acquired 100% of Richards Manufacturing Co. (“Richards Manufacturing”), a U.S.-based producer of overhead and underground electrical and gas distribution products, for cash of approximately $2.3 billion, net of cash acquired.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated because the anchor contains only partial-year acquired results. Richards' filed pro-forma net-income effect was small, but the filing does not provide full owner-earnings components for Richards and the other acquisitions. The record therefore cannot establish the net OE effect or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Construct full-year pro-forma OE for all FY2025 acquisitions, including sustainable operating profit, cash taxes, financing cost, maintenance capital, working-capital requirements, eligible amortization, and recurring integration costs; then rerun the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Restructuring appears recurring rather than exceptional
audit_findings.magnitude: $96m of restructuring charges in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, approximately $100m expected full-year charges and $110m expected cash spending; a $100m recurring adjustment equals 4.48% of anchor OE and approximately $4.71 per base-case share if capitalized proportionally
audit_findings.mechanism: An improper recurring-cost add-back overstates normalized OE and all scenario operating values.
audit_findings.evidence: For fiscal 2026, we expect total restructuring charges to be approximately $100 million and total spending, which will be funded with cash from operations, to be approximately $100 million.
audit_findings.explanation: Recurrence is demonstrated by charges across successive programs, while the OE treatment is unresolved. Even a conservative dollar-for-dollar $100m reduction to sustainable OE would lower base value from $109.14 to about $104.43 per share, without changing the valuation conclusion relative to the $209.58 price.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every annual OE reconciliation for restructuring add-backs; retain recurring cash spending and ensure productivity savings are not credited while their enabling costs are removed.

audit_findings.title: The historical tax anchor may not capture the new global minimum tax regime
audit_findings.mechanism: A higher sustainable post-Pillar-Two cash-tax burden would reduce forecast OE and potentially the sustainable growth supported by retained earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Ireland has implemented elements of the OECD’s global minimum tax rules, which were effective for us beginning in fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The regime has been effective since fiscal 2025, so this is a present normalization issue rather than solely a future risk. The filed 15% minimum rate, the 23.0% latest-quarter effective rate, and the 18.1% nine-month rate containing a $114m settlement benefit do not isolate recurring Pillar-Two cash taxes. The record therefore cannot establish materiality. The separate $574m deferred-tax valuation-allowance charge is noncash and does not resolve the recurring cash-tax question.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a jurisdiction-level post-Pillar-Two cash-tax forecast, exclude the $574m valuation-allowance charge and settlement benefits, reconcile it to normalized OE, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2018 residual $172.0m, equal to 25.8% of filed D&A and 9.55% of FY2018 OE; other-year and anchor effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic expense would be added back to annual OE and could alter the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2018 $172.0m (25.8% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: There is no demonstrated overstatement because the unidentified amount remains expensed. The FY2018 amount establishes possible understatement in that year, but one observation does not establish the effect on the ten-year regression anchor, and corresponding residual amounts for other years are not supplied. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Classify residual D&A by asset and economic purpose for every anchor year, add back only components supported as non-economic, and rerun the complete OE series and log-trend anchor.
